answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a zephyr as the anchor of the cost.
